pages.text: "A little longer..." Mina, a handspan taller than Sonu, pulled the quilt over their head. Overnight, the river had fallen to reveal two more steps. Round-bellied little Sonu shook Mina. "Let's see the waterbirds!"
"I want to see white birds sitting on the steps, too..." Mina mumbled, curling up and staying still. Sonu went to the yard alone.
Much later, Mina opened their eyes in surprise. The sun was high above the river. Not a bird sat on the steps. "Did they all fly away?" Mina pouted.
Mom sat beside Mina inside. "They sit on the steps only when the sun rises over the river." She held both hands and stretched them up together.
Hands stretched, feet stretched, the whole body lengthened. Mina's eyes opened wide. "Stretching wakes me up!" Pushing away the quilt, Mina called, "Sun Comes Up, Quilt Off—Stretch!"
Mom leaned toward the door and whispered, "Go say good morning to the sun." Mina opened the door and hopped into the yard. A morning breeze drifted in.
Mina spread both hands. "Hello, sun! Sun Comes Up, Quilt Off—Stretch!" Sonu copied beside the water tub.
Mom scooped water with a dipper. "Cold water on your face opens your eyes all the way." Mina splashed their face. Their cheeks felt clean.
The next day, Mina pushed the quilt away and stretched. "Sonu, let's see the birds!" On the steps they reached with Mom, white birds sat in a row.
Mom hugged Mina from behind. Pointing, Mina whispered, "I didn't miss them today."
